clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather's return to the family in early 1989 and through the months after your grandfather Gordon died in June 1991, shifts piled up: you liked late nights and dropped chess and debate; you leaned hard on Rafe once at conservatory, then clashed with him after a wrist injury stopped your playing; you were lost and low with your grandfather gone and your mother about to remarry; you sank into fixing radios and later a bleak year at community college. Your father came back into the family around the same time your grandfather died. By early 1994, when you were stung that your dad had never heard of your film, the acute upheaval had settled into a steadier state, though the shifts show your functioning down and your anxiety up across those years.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's cancer diagnosis, 2001–2003
clusters.reason: Around the time your grandmother was found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002, alongside your disastrous audition and your running out of steam for performing, you were on poor terms with family and friends; you left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, met Marisol there, moved to live with her in Fenwick, then split up within the year and sank into deep depression once back in Thornbury. You could not face your family and relied on friends instead. These months show you shifting away from your parents and toward friends, your functioning down, your anxiety up. Your grandmother spent her final months in your parents' home that autumn.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around the time your grandmother died in January 2008 and your grandfather that same month or near it, you took four weeks building at Alder Creek with Silas in July; there your mother pressed to visit you repeatedly, you kept the door shut on her, and you stopped speaking to her when you left for nursing school that August. The shifts show distance and conflict between you and your mother during those months, and then cutoff once you moved to Marlow Sound. The silence held for roughly a year.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017 and through October 2019, shifts piled up close together: you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along; your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in October 2017; by October 2019 Wren was swamped one thing after another, you were too strict laying out a plan to settle her, she talked with her father and brother all day, and at her mother's retirement party at the lake house you were awake from the small hours with no more sleep, could only pull back as the others rose, and felt you didn't belong. Wren was anxious when you'd had no sleep at family occasions. The shifts show your anxiety and symptom up, your functioning down at times, and relationship shifts between you and Wren and between you and her family, with distance when you are among them.
